title: How he got the name Butter in McKinney's band
summary: Don Redman nicknamed him Butter because he looked tender and plump when he joined McKinney's Cotton Pickers on December 7, 1930.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: I just want to get back to a little bit of the early days first. You've given me a lot of things about the different members of the orchestra.
Let me ask you, how did you, how did the name Butter -- how did you get that name?
Oh, Don Redman when I first joined McKinney's Cottonpickers, I was young and I looked tender, you know, --
No, no. I joined McKinney's Cottonpickers December 7, 1930.
And they looked at me and, I don't know, they looked at me and I don't know whether my complexion had anything to do with it or not, but Don said I looked like butter.
Ah, ha, ha, ha. It was the complexion, yeah.
And I was plump, too, you know. Being plump and all that, you know, I was -- oh, I weighed about 210 then, you know. And, gee whiz, I was 20---- when I joined that band I was 21 years old, --
